To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heterophilic interactions of nectins in concert with the classical cadherin machinery play a pivotal role in the selective recognition of axons and their dendritic partners.

the axon-dendrite specificity of nectin interactions is critical for the formation of interaxonal connections and that nectins cooperate with the cadherins for the regulation of interneurite affinity.
the heterophilic interaction of N1 and N3 in concert with the activity of cadherin–β-catenin complex plays a critical role in interneuronal recognition and in the ordered association of neurites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the formation of interaxonal and interdendritic contacts.
the molecular mechanism underlying the recognition and attachment of axons and their specific partners, which are crucial steps in neuronal connectivity and synaptogenesis.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the formation of specific interneuronal associations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nectins are essential to regulate the interneuronal interactions in concert with cadherins.
the heterophilic interactions of N1 and N3 in concert with the activity of the cadherin–cadherin adhesion machinery regulate the selective association of axons with dendrites.
the axon-dendrite recognition mechanism is a result of the interplay among nectins, cadherin, and their downstream signaling pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heterophilic nects and the cadherin–cadherin adhesion systems are functionally linked to regulate interneurite specificity.
the axon–dendrite affinity is determined by the differential localization of N1 in axons, the trans-interaction of N3 with N1 on the opposite neurite, and the cadherin-mediated neurite adhesion.

the axon-dendrite recognition is regulated by a balance between the cadherin and nectin systems, and the cadherin system is more dominant in the axon-dentritic recognition than that of the dendrite-dendritic recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nectins play a critical role in regulating neurite affinity by modulating the adhesive properties of cadherin-based cell–cell junctions.
the heterophilic nects are involved in interneuronal recognition and that they cooperate with the cadherins to regulate the formation of specific connections between axons and their targets.
nectin-1 is a key molecule for the recognition of axon-dendritic connections.
